# Molecular cloning of htra2-beta-1 and htra2-beta-2, two human homologs of tra-2 generated by alternative splicing.
**Authors:** Beil B, Screaton G, Stamm S
**Journal:** DNA Cell Biol (1997)
**DOI:** [10.1089/dna.1997.16.679](https://doi.org/10.1089/dna.1997.16.679)

## Abstract

1. DNA Cell Biol. 1997 Jun;16(6):679-90. doi: 10.1089/dna.1997.16.679.

Molecular cloning of htra2-beta-1 and htra2-beta-2, two human homologs of tra-2 
generated by alternative splicing.

Beil B(1), Screaton G, Stamm S.

Author information:
(1)Max-Planck Institute for Psychiatry, Planegg, Germany.

A yeast two-hybrid screen was performed to find new factors involved in pre-mRNA 
splicing. Using SC35 as a bait, we isolated a human cDNA bearing high homology 
to the Drosophila transformer-2 (TRA-2) protein. This cDNA was named 
htra2-beta1. htra2-beta1 is a nuclear protein that colocalizes with SC35 in a 
speckled pattern. It interacts with several SR proteins tested in yeast. A 
second form named htra2-beta2 is generated by alternative splicing. This isoform 
gives rise to a truncated protein without an SR domain. Both isoforms are evenly 
distributed throughout adult rat tissue. The ratio of these two isoforms changes 
after stimulation of primary human T-cell and primary rat spleen cell cultures, 
indicating that alternative splicing is involved in regulation of htra2-beta 
activity.
